findings: The candidate accurately depicts an adult American Herring Gull in nonbreeding plumage: robust gull proportions, pale-gray mantle, white underparts, gray-brown head and neck streaking, pale iris, yellow bill with a red gonys spot, dull-pink legs, and black wingtips with white markings.

The primary specimen has one head, one bill, a convincing complete pair of folded wings, two attached legs with intact feet, and one tail; far-side structures are naturally overlapped rather than duplicated or detached.

Both adult bill depictions now show a clearly hooked upper mandible projecting materially beyond the lower mandible, consistent with the clearest side-profile reference. The earlier correction has not regressed.
The detached wing and head are clearly supplementary studies and do not appear attached to the primary specimen. Their anatomy and plumage are consistent with the species.
All visible headings, names, measurements, field marks, habitat text, behavior text, and palette labels are legible and faithfully reproduce the proposed profile.
Audubon directly supports the displayed measurement set: length 56–66 cm, wingspan 120–150 cm, and weight 800–1,250 g, with sexes similar.

The vertical length diagram increases from 56 cm at the bottom to 66 cm at the top, agrees with the printed body-length range, uses centimeters consistently, and is explicitly labeled “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE.”
The plate contains no place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail.
